user.title: Set up UK Journey Guardian
user.description: Connect a travel calendar, routing providers, and destination zones. Credentials are stored by Home Assistant and are never exposed as entity state.

data.station_access_mode: Default way to reach the station

data_description.calendar_entity: Calendar containing timed rail journey events.
data_description.calendar_refresh_interval_minutes: How often Journey Guardian asks Home Assistant to update the selected calendar from its upstream source. Daily is the default. Disabled leaves refresh timing entirely to the calendar integration.
data_description.person_entity: Person whose location will be used for travel decisions.
data_description.home_zone: Zone used to identify home departures.
data_description.destination_zones: Optional zones representing one or more regular destinations.
data_description.preparation_buffer_minutes: Minutes allowed to get ready before leaving for the station.
data_description.early_warning_minutes: Additional conservative margin before preparation should begin.
data_description.station_buffer_minutes: Minutes to arrive at the station before the scheduled train departure.
data_description.station_access_fallback_minutes: Minutes allowed to reach the station until live routing is available. Timing is labelled inferred.
data_description.station_access_minimum_minutes: Minimum door-to-station allowance retained when live routing reports a shorter trip. Include parking, walking, and other fixed overhead.
data_description.station_access_mode: Default for stations without a profile. Automatic selects driving at home and public transport while away.
data_description.station_access_profiles: Optional: one CRS=mode per line, such as SMP=transit. To use an existing Waze sensor: EXC|Example Central=waze:sensor.example_route. The optional exact station name matches calendars without CRS codes. Unmatched stations use the default.
data_description.transportapi_app_id: Optional until TransportAPI rail monitoring is enabled.
data_description.transportapi_app_key: Optional until TransportAPI rail monitoring is enabled. Stored privately in the Home Assistant config entry.
data_description.live_rail_provider: TransportAPI uses the configured daily credit limit. Railinfo is keyless and uses its separate fair-use allowance, with the same bounded checkpoint schedule.
data_description.google_routes_api_key: Optional until Google routing is enabled. Use a dedicated restricted server-side Routes API key.
data_description.daily_api_limit: Maximum TransportAPI calls permitted each local day.
data_description.delay_repay_threshold_minutes: Confirmed destination delay required before Journey Guardian raises a possible compensation claim.
data_description.urgent_api_reserve: Routine checks stop before consuming this final reserve.
data_description.automatic_live_rail_enabled: Off by default. When enabled, Journey Guardian makes one quota-controlled live rail check at each planned checkpoint.
data_description.live_notifications_enabled: Off by default during shadow testing. Simulations can still create test notifications.
data_description.announcement_text_entity: Input text helper that receives the rendered announcement before the script runs.
data_description.announcement_script_entity: Script called after the announcement text helper has been updated.
data_description.home_wake_enabled: Off by default for new installations. Existing installations with an announcement script keep the repeating alarm enabled when upgraded.
data_description.home_wake_awake_entity: Optional binary sensor or input boolean that stops the repeating alarm when the traveller is awake. Without one, the alarm continues until another safety stop.
data_description.home_wake_awake_state: Choose whether on or off from the evidence entity means the traveller is awake.
data_description.home_wake_repeat_seconds: Seconds between home wake-up announcements. Six seconds produces up to ten announcements per minute.
data_description.home_wake_max_minutes: Safety limit for one home wake-up alarm. It also stops at the leave-home time, when the traveller leaves home, or when awake evidence appears.

error.reserve_must_be_lower: The urgent reserve must be lower than the daily limit.
error.invalid_station_access_profiles: Use unique CRS=mode or CRS|Station name=waze:sensor.entity entries. Modes: driving, walking, bicycling, transit.
error.duplicate_station_access_profile: Each station can appear only once.

abort.already_configured: UK Journey Guardian is already configured.

error.invalid_progress_zones: Enter 2 to 100 unique zone entity IDs, one per line, or leave blank to disable progress.
error.invalid_progress_alternatives: Enter up to four paths, one per line: base start > extra station > base end. Anchors must follow base order; extra stations must be unique. Maximum 100 stations in total.

init.title: Journey settings
init.description: Edit conservative timing, notifications, and the live rail provider.

data.station_access_mode: Default way to reach the station

data_description.preparation_buffer_minutes: Minutes allowed to get ready before leaving for the station.
data_description.progress_zones: Optional: one zone entity ID per line in route order (2 to 100 unique stations). Blank disables GPS progress. Zone names must match calendar endpoints; a leading zzz prefix followed by a space is ignored. Return legs reverse the route automatically.
data_description.progress_alternatives: Optional: one path per line, separated by >. Start and finish each path with stations on the ordered base route; place diversion stations between them. Fresh GPS selects a path, never a timetable assumption.
data_description.calendar_refresh_interval_minutes: How often Journey Guardian asks Home Assistant to update the selected calendar from its upstream source. The manual refresh button always forces an update.
data_description.early_warning_minutes: Additional conservative margin before preparation should begin.
data_description.station_buffer_minutes: Minutes to arrive at the station before the scheduled train departure.
data_description.station_access_fallback_minutes: Minutes allowed to reach the station until live routing is available. Timing is labelled inferred.
data_description.station_access_minimum_minutes: Minimum door-to-station allowance retained when live routing reports a shorter trip. Include parking, walking, and other fixed overhead.
data_description.station_access_mode: Choose the default for stations without a profile. Use profiles for regular exceptions such as EXC=driving.
data_description.station_access_profiles: One CRS=mode per line, such as SMP=transit. For an existing Waze sensor: EXC|Example Central=waze:sensor.example_route. The optional exact station name matches calendars without CRS codes. A Waze profile never silently switches to Google.
data_description.automatic_live_rail_enabled: Runs restart-safe, quota-controlled checks from 150 minutes to 1 minute before departure, plus one 15-minute post-departure check.
data_description.live_notifications_enabled: Off keeps real calendar journeys in shadow mode while allowing simulation notifications.
data_description.delay_repay_threshold_minutes: Confirmed destination delay required before the nightly review raises a possible compensation claim.
data_description.announcement_text_entity: Select the input text helper used by your announcement engine.
data_description.announcement_script_entity: Select the script that delivers the announcement after the helper is updated.
data_description.home_wake_enabled: When enabled, the first preparation alert repeats while the traveller remains at home. Live notifications and an announcement script must also be enabled for phone or watch delivery.
data_description.home_wake_awake_entity: Optional: select a binary sensor or input boolean that changes when you are awake. Leave blank to repeat until the safety limit, leave-home time, journey change, or departure from home.
data_description.home_wake_awake_state: Choose whether on or off means awake for the selected evidence entity.
data_description.home_wake_repeat_seconds: Seconds between home wake-up announcements. The default is six seconds, or up to ten announcements per minute.
data_description.home_wake_max_minutes: Safety limit for the repeating alarm. It stops earlier on awake evidence, leaving home, a journey change, or the leave-home time.
data_description.transportapi_app_id: Required for manual or automatic live-rail checks. Leave blank to keep the saved value; a new value replaces it.
data_description.transportapi_app_key: Required for manual or automatic live-rail checks. Leave blank to keep the saved value; a new value replaces it.
data_description.live_rail_provider: Railinfo needs no credentials and does not consume the TransportAPI budget. Its use remains bounded by Journey Guardian's checkpoint schedule and provider rate-limit back-off.
data_description.google_routes_api_key: Optional Google Routes key for live station-access timing. Leave blank to keep the saved value; a new value replaces it.

travel_review_now.name: Travel review now
travel_review_now.description: Refresh the calendar, station access and eligible live rail data, then send a briefing. Repeated taps within 30 seconds reuse the result.

notify.name: Send briefing
notify.description: Send the summary through the configured announcement script and keep the full report in Home Assistant. Disable for response-only use.

review_now.name: Review journey now
review_now.description: Immediately refresh the calendar and UK Journey Guardian decision path.

review_rail_now.name: Check live rail now
review_rail_now.description: Explicitly check the selected live rail provider for the current calendar journey. TransportAPI can consume its configured allowance; Railinfo uses its separate fair-use allowance.

simulate_journey.name: Simulate journey
simulate_journey.description: Activate a deterministic journey scenario without contacting TransportAPI or consuming provider allowance.

scenario.name: Scenario
scenario.description: Synthetic rail condition to apply until simulation is cleared or Home Assistant restarts.

departure_in_minutes.name: Departure in minutes
departure_in_minutes.description: Minutes from now to the synthetic scheduled departure.

delay_minutes.name: Delay minutes
delay_minutes.description: Delay applied by the delayed scenario; ignored by other scenarios.

duration_minutes.name: Journey duration
duration_minutes.description: Duration of the synthetic journey after its effective departure.

accelerated.name: Accelerated timeline
accelerated.description: Compress preparation, access, and station stages into minutes for rapid end-to-end testing.

clear_simulation.name: Clear simulation
clear_simulation.description: Return Journey Guardian to its configured calendar source. No provider call is made.

sustained_calendar.title: Journey Guardian cannot refresh its calendar
sustained_calendar.description: Calendar reviews have failed repeatedly for at least 30 minutes. Check the selected calendar and its upstream source, then use Refresh calendar and timings. Recovered booked intent is not confirmation that the calendar is current. Keep an independent travel alarm. This notice clears after a successful review.

sustained_routing.title: Journey Guardian is using fallback station-access timing
sustained_routing.description: Station-access routing has failed repeatedly for at least 30 minutes. Check the Station access routing source/error attributes. For Waze, check the selected local duration sensor and its freshness. For Google, check API access, restrictions, billing and quota. Journey Guardian is using the configured conservative allowance, not a live estimate. This notice clears after a successful route calculation.

sustained_rail.title: Journey Guardian cannot obtain current rail status
sustained_rail.description: Live rail checks have failed repeatedly for at least 30 minutes. Check the provider configuration, credentials, allowance and the Status entity's last live rail error. Do not reset the stored budget to bypass limits. Retained observations are not current railway confirmation. This notice clears after a successful live rail check.
